questions.q: Which chart title best follows the 'title the finding' rule?
options: Churn rate by support tickets
Customers with 3+ tickets churn about 4x as often
Figure 3
Ticket counts and churn (bar chart)
questions.explain: A good title states what the reader should conclude, not just which variables are plotted.

questions.q: In the context, tension, resolution structure, which part is 'Churn climbs steeply with support contacts'?
options: Resolution
Context
Appendix
Tension
questions.explain: Tension is the surprising or important pattern. Context is the baseline; resolution is what to do about it.

questions.q: In the lesson's code, why is support_tickets clipped at 3?
options: So the last bar groups everyone with 3 or more tickets, keeping the chart to four clear bars
Because pandas cannot plot more than four bars
To remove customers with many tickets from the dataset
To make the churn rate look bigger
questions.explain: clip(upper=3) turns every count above 3 into 3, so the final bar means '3 or more'.

questions.q: The rates were 11.3% for zero tickets and 44.7% for three or more. Where does 'about 4x' come from?
options: The difference, 44.7 minus 11.3
The average of the four bars
The ratio 44.7 divided by 11.3, which is 4.0
The number of ticket groups
questions.explain: Compute the number you quote: 44.7 / 11.3 = 4.0 in the run we made.

questions.q: Which claim is most appropriately hedged given only this chart?
options: Support tickets cause customers to leave
Reducing tickets will cut churn by 75%
High-ticket customers churn more often; the data alone does not show that tickets cause it
Churn is a solved problem
questions.explain: The chart shows an association. Unhappy customers may both complain and leave, so causation is not established.
